entries.title: Obadiah 1:1
segments: Is sent among the heathen; to stir them up to war against Edom. His words follow immediately.

entries.title: Obadiah 1:2
segments: I have made thee small; the future punishment of Edom is spoken of as if it had already taken place.  Compare
.  Some think the sins of Edom, described

, are in like manner future, though the spirit which prompts to them already exists, and manifests itself as it has opportunity. 
 
vv 2-4. 
 
No wisdom, riches , military power, or natural strength of position, can secure a people against God's judgments.  When a nation puts its trust in these, instead of its Maker, and is thus lifted up with pride and self-confidence, God will make it "small" and "greatly despised" before the eyes of all men.

entries.title: Obadiah 1:3
segments:
vv 3-4. 
 
  The pride of thy heart--bring thee down; see note on

entries.title: Obadiah 1:5
segments:
Till they had enough; that is, only till they had enough, leaving the rest. 
 
  Grape-gatherers; a symbol for "thieves" and "robbers," Edom being the plundered vine.  The meaning of these questions is, that the enemies of Edom have ravaged her more than thieves and robbers. Compare

entries.title: Obadiah 1:6
segments: Searched out--sought up; by his enemies.

entries.title: Obadiah 1:7
segments:
Men of thy confederacy; Edom's allies, to whom he trusted for help. 
 
  A wound; or, "a snare." 
 
  In him; in Edom. 
 
The confederacies which one wicked nation makes with neighboring nations as wicked as itself, will in the end bring destruction instead of salvation.

entries.title: Obadiah 1:8
segments:
vv 8-9. 
 
  Wise men--mighty men--Teman; see

. 
 
When God purposes to destroy a nation for its sins, he commonly removes from it the wise and prudent, and gives it over to weak and foolish counsels.

entries.title: Obadiah 1:10
segments:
vv 10-16. 
 
To rejoice over the calamities which befall our enemies is a heinous sin, which God will not suffer to go unpunished; but when the wicked exult in the sufferings which he sends upon his own people for their correction, and aggravate them by deeds of cruelty and perfidy, he will put to their lips the cup of wrath, and compel them to drink it to the dregs.

entries.title: Obadiah 1:11
segments:
His forces--his gates; those of God's people. 
 
  Wast as one of them; see

entries.title: Obadiah 1:12
segments: Thou shouldest not have looked; rather, "do not behold;" and so of all the other expressions to the end of
.  Thus the prophet warns Edom against indulging his hatred towards God's people.

entries.title: Obadiah 1:14
segments: Delivered up; to the enemy.

entries.title: Obadiah 1:16
segments: As ye have drunk upon my holy mountain; as ye, my people, who dwell upon my holy mountain, have drunk; that is, drunk the cup of my wrath. Compare
.  For the doctrine here taught, compare

entries.title: Obadiah 1:17
segments:
Their possessions; the possessions of the Edomites. 
 
vv 17-21. 
 
When God afflicts his covenant people, it is always for their purification and salvation; in due time he grants them, through Christ, a glorious deliverance from their troubles, and makes them victorious over all that hated and persecuted them.

entries.title: Obadiah 1:19
segments:
They of the south; they of Judah, who occupy the south of Palestine, shall possess the mount of Esau; which extended south and east of the southern border of Judah. 
 
  They of the plain;  of Judah, towards the Mediterranean, shall possess the land of the Philistines; which lay on the western border of this plain: they shall possess Ephraim and Samaria; that is, the territory of the kingdom of Israel.  Thus the whole of Canaan is given to Judah. 
 
  Gilead; on the east of the Jordan, opposite to the territory of Benjamin.

entries.title: Obadiah 1:20
segments:
The captivity--of Israel; the remnant of the ten tribes are assigned a portion out of Palestine, adjacent to their ancient territory in Palestine. 
 
  That of the Canaanites; the territory of the Canaanites, north of the ancient possessions of Israel. 
 
  Zarephath; on the sea-coast of Phenicia, between Tyre and Zidon. 
 
  The captivity--in Sepharad; captives from Jerusalem, then dwelling in Sepharad; of these and of Sepharad we know nothing. 
 
  The cities of the south; heathen cities, apparently beyond "the mount of Esau," which has been given to the south of Judah,

; just as the captivity of Israel has a possession north of that given to Judah. 
 
In interpreting this and the preceding verse, we are not to insist on particulars.  The meaning is, that the remnant of Judah and Israel shall possess the land of their enemies; and this, again, represents the universal spiritual triumph of God's people.

entries.title: Obadiah 1:21
segments: Saviors; in the temporal saviors after the Babylonish captivity, who conquered the Edomites, we have only the earnest of the true fulfilment of this promise in Christ.
